results.title: BoE Systemic Risk Survey results – H1 2026
results.content: Tracks financial services regulatory developments and provides insight and commentary. ## BoE Systemic Risk Survey results – H1 2026. On 1 April 2026, the Bank of England issued its Systemic Risk Survey results for H1 2026. The Systemic Risk Survey is conducted on a biannual basis, to quantify and track market participants’ views of risks to, and their confidence in, the stability of the UK financial system. The H1 survey was conducted between 19 January and 16 February 2026 and 57 firms participated in it, representing a 66% response rate. Our blog, Global Regulation Tomorrow offers a convenient resource for those keeping track of the evolving and increasingly complex global financial services regulatory environment. It reports on financial services regulatory developments and provides insights and commentary across Africa, Asia, Australia, Canada, Europe and the United States. We cover a broad range of financial services regulatory topics including banking and capital adequacy regulation, clearing and settlement, anti-money laundering, insurance, regulation and compliance retail and wholesale conduct and securities regulation.

results.title: Homogeneity of corporate risk perceptions and systemic financial risk
results.content: Panel regression analysis has verified a positive relationship between the homogeneity of risk perception among financial institutions and the extent of systemic risk. Section 4 illustrates the measures of risk perception homogeneity among financial institutions based on their textual risk disclosures, followed by the description of systemic risk measures, regression models. Methodologically, by measuring interconnectedness based on the homogeneity of risks perceived by financial institutions, this paper provides novel evidence on the relationship between interconnectedness and systemic risk, offering a fresh perspective rooted in corporate risk perception. This indicates that the banks generally have high homogeneity with other financial institutions regarding corporate risk perception. This indicates that increased connectedness, measured by greater homogeneity in risk perception among financial institutions, will exacerbate systemic risk. The empirical results, as tabulated in Tables 5 and 6, demonstrate that, irrespective of whether within banking or non-banking sectors, a surge in risk perception homogeneity of financial institutions is correlated with a pronounced escalation in systemic risk.
